root_cause.text: In net/rds, rds_message_purge() incorrectly used rm->m_rs to infer zerocopy ownership instead of the op_mmp_znotifier state, so a zerocopy send that failed before socket queue attachment was cleaned up via the normal payload-page path despite still owning pinned user pages.
root_cause.evidence: The commit message states “The purge path currently infers zerocopy state from rm->m_rs” and that “zerocopy ownership is really determined by the presence of op_mmp_znotifier”; the patch captures rm->data.op_mmp_znotifier up front, handles the rm->m_rs == NULL && znotifier case by calling mm_unaccount_pinned_pages() and freeing the notifier, instead of treating it like a non-zerocopy message.

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix rds_message_purge() to properly detach and clean up zerocopy notifier resources even when a message has no associated socket.
intent_record.what: The function rds_message_purge() now declares a local struct rds_znotifier *znotifier, initializes it under rm->m_rs_lock from rm->data.op_mmp_znotifier, clears rm->data.op_mmp_znotifier immediately, and sets zcopy based on whether znotifier is non-NULL. The previous inline checks of rm->data.op_mmp_znotifier inside the rm->m_rs branch are replaced with checks against the local znotifier variable. A new else-if branch was added for the case where rm->m_rs is NULL but znotifier exists, calling mm_unaccount_pinned_pages(&znotifier->z_mmp) and kfree(rds_info_from_znotifier(znotifier)).
intent_record.how: At runtime, zerocopy notification state is detached from the message while holding the lock, avoiding repeated direct access to the shared field and ensuring it is cleared consistently. If the message still has an associated socket, the existing zerocopy callback and wakeup behavior still occur using the saved notifier. If zerocopy setup failed before the message was queued on a socket, the new NULL-rs path now releases pinned-page accounting and frees the notifier instead of leaving those resources unreleased.

grouping_result.intent: Fix rds_message_purge() to properly detach and clean up zerocopy notifier resources even when a message has no associated socket.

relevance_review.reason: The change directly fixes rds_message_purge() cleanup logic for zerocopy notifier resources when no socket is attached, matching the root cause of using the wrong ownership signal and mishandling failed zerocopy sends before socket queue attachment.

candidates.rationale: This conditional gates zerocopy cleanup on the presence of an attached socket, embodying the bug described in the root cause: ownership/cleanup of zerocopy resources was inferred from rm->m_rs rather than the zerocopy notifier state, so failed zerocopy sends without socket attachment skipped the zerocopy path.

vuln_statements.explanation: This conditional selected the zerocopy cleanup path based on whether the message had an associated socket (rm->m_rs) instead of whether zerocopy notifier ownership existed. As a result, zerocopy sends that failed before socket queue attachment skipped the notifier cleanup path and were purged as normal payload pages despite still owning pinned user pages.

bic_trace_step.reason: The relevant cleanup function is present and fully visible, so the snippet is sufficient. In this commit, `rds_message_purge()` only does generic payload cleanup: it returns early for `RDS_MSG_PAGEVEC`, otherwise loops over `rm->m_nents` and frees each page with `__free_page(sg_page(&rm->m_sg[i]));`, then frees `rm->m_rdma_op` and `rm->m_rdma_mr` if present. However, the vulnerability described depends specifically on `rds_message_purge()` incorrectly using `rm->m_rs` to infer zerocopy ownership instead of `op_mmp_znotifier` state. In this function body, there is no reference to `rm->m_rs`, no zerocopy-specific ownership check, and no `op_mmp_znotifier` handling at all. Because the vulnerable construct is completely absent from this early version of the function, `has_bug` must be false. At the same time, the later fix is also not present, since there is likewise no correct zerocopy cleanup logic based on notifier state.
